newsitem.title: UK: UK TV watchdog approves greater tele-shopping.
newsitem.headline: UK TV watchdog approves greater tele-shopping.

text.p: Britain's television watchdog on Wednesday said it approved changes that will allow cable, satellite and new digital channels to carry additional tele-shopping advertising and open the way to the licensing of self-promotional channels.

The Independent Television Commission (ITC), the regulator for Britain's commercial television channels, said the changes reflect provisions of the revised European Union Directive on Television Without Frontiers adopted on Wednesday.

The EU Directive was revised to permit up to three hours per day of tele-shopping windows. A window is an advertisement that lasts a minimum of 15 minutes. Tele-shopping includes home shopping channels, infomercials and advertorials. The allowance is in addition to existing amounts of advertising and tele-shopping spots, the ITC said.

A self-promotional channel is a form of an all-advertising channel where the broadcast promotes its own products, services or channels. The ITC said that under the new rules a computer company, for example, could apply for a licence in order to showcase its own computers and software
The ITC said its changes do not affect existing regulations on advertising and tele-shopping on Britain's three commercial terrestrial channels: the ITV, Channel 4 and Channel 5.
